votes.reasoning: The finding's four points are each addressed. (1) Flight semantics are documented at SingleFlight.swift:14-22. (2) The dead checkCancellation inside the refresh flight was removed, and the check moved to after refreshAndWriteBack (AnthropicProvider.swift:101; OpenAIProvider.swift:79 and :95). The rotated token is therefore always written back before the caller aborts. (3) The gate is held for the whole dialog, and this is now documented (KeychainCredentialReader.swift:88). (4) OffPool tests moved to their own file, and the detached task in VendorSectionView was dropped because authorizeCredentialsOffPool already hops to GCD. The Ferreiro's mutation check covers SingleFlightTests; I did not re-run that particular mutation. The test passes on the current tree.

SingleFlight.swift:13-22 documents the design choice instead of adding cancellation plumbing. The in-flight checkCancellation calls, which could never fire, were removed from AnthropicProvider.swift:124 and OpenAIProvider.swift:118, and caller-side checks were added after refreshAndWriteBack. That also satisfies the 'check after OAuth refresh' hard rule. The now-redundant Task.detached was removed from VendorSectionView.swift:421. The OffPool tests moved to their own Tests/AiTaskbarCoreTests/OffPoolTests.swift. The gate comment at KeychainCredentialReader.swift:88 states why the lock is held. No new swallowed errors or wrappers were introduced.

The finding lists four items, and each maps to a change: SingleFlight.swift:13-22 documents the by-design non-cancellation; KeychainCredentialReader.swift:88 explains why the gate is held; OffPoolTests.swift is split out of SingleFlightTests; VendorSectionView.swift:418 drops the redundant Task.detached. The in-flight checkCancellation moves to after run returns (AnthropicProvider.swift:101, OpenAIProvider.swift:79/95), which still satisfies the hard rule to check after OAuth refresh.
